paper_id: Wang et al. - 2012 - Triggercast Enabling Wireless Collisions Constructive
title: Triggercast: Enabling Wireless Collisions Constructive
motivation: Concurrent transmissions waste energy; CI promises N²-fold power gain
problem_framing: Achieve CI in WSNs via chip-level sync and SNR-constrained link selection
key_insight: Perfect chip sync insufficient; must satisfy SNR ratio bounds and phase constraints
method_signature: CLS + LSA algorithms compensate delay and select co-senders for CI
evaluation_criteria: PRR improvements (5%→70%), RSSI gains, 250ns sync accuracy
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: NDI provides no guarantee of power gains; more senders can degrade PRR
evidence_for_taste: NDI provides no guarantee of power gains
more senders might degrade PRR significantly
capture effect dominates the packet reception
The accuracy is bounded by the running frequency
even perfectly aligned signals with different link qualities might also superpose destructively
thinking_moves: 从工程异常反推底层假设失效：实验发现NDI不保证功率增益，推翻盲目并发假设
理论最坏情况推导：证明完美chip同步仍可能CI失效，需SNR比值约束
物理层约束→系统算法：把时延补偿和链路选择形式化为可求解问题
承认硬件硬边界：同步精度受MCU频率限制，而非算法不足
cites_own_work: Wang et al., 2012 - Exploiting Constructive Interference for Scalable Flooding in Wireless Networks (IEEE INFOCOM)
